_comment: Hand-maintained. These lists cannot be derived from the repos or the tracker:
a decision and its rejected alternative live in issue prose, not in structured fields.
Every entry cites an issue and carries reviewed_at, the date a person last checked it
against that issue. tools/build_analysis.py compares the two and reports drift; it
never rewrites an entry. See ANALYSIS.md for the review procedure.

decisions.title: Hub plus Hosted Control Planes
decisions.rejected: A dedicated control plane per cluster
decisions.why: Hardware efficiency and fast cluster creation; the hub becomes the critical control point

decisions.title: Two-stage build: dev on ESI, prod on dedicated hardware
decisions.why: RHOSO was not ready and the stack had to be proven quickly

decisions.title: Keycloak as the sole IdP, federated via CILogon
decisions.rejected: A separate IdP for the NIST environment
decisions.why: One identity platform; a single option holds under 800-171

decisions.title: Keycloak on AWS EKS in the MOC account, as a pilot
decisions.why: The IdP must survive a cluster outage; reuses Kubernetes skills; compliance deferred

decisions.title: Argo CD + Helm + ACM Placements instead of ai-ivp
decisions.why: Simpler and offers more control over what is deployed

decisions.title: Only pre-registered users may authenticate, on every cluster
decisions.rejected: The MOC 1.0 model: anyone may log in, with no privileges
decisions.why: NIST requires it and there is a single login front end

decisions.title: S3 through an in-cluster reverse proxy on a Multus storage network
decisions.rejected: Host routing, per-namespace attachments, default-gateway routing
decisions.why: Keeps the fast storage path with minimal tenant configuration and no route leakage

decisions.title: No RDMA or SR-IOV for the Open Accelerator
decisions.why: Not needed by current workloads; the capability stays available but unenabled

decisions.title: Tenant projects from a Git values file, not ColdFront
decisions.why: Saves engineering time for the NIST build

decisions.title: Three-tier ANP / NetworkPolicy / BANP tenant isolation
decisions.why: One tier cannot express both an admin guarantee and tenant flexibility

decisions.title: HAProxy on the firewall for hosted-cluster endpoints
decisions.why: Simpler for services that are NodePorts anyway

decisions.title: GPUs billed by requested capacity: the status quo, not yet a decision
decisions.rejected: Nothing yet: D1 (requested capacity, usage-based, or a tier model) is still open
decisions.why: It is what is implemented today (kube_pod_resource_request). The RfD asks MOC leadership to decide D1 and recommends the tier model; no decision has been written back into the issue.

decisions.title: COSI driver for S3 bucket management on Pure
decisions.rejected: An admission webhook creating users, keys and quotas against the Pure API
decisions.why: The free Portworx px-csi has no CRD-based way to manage buckets; start with an in-house COSI driver, then the vendor's

decisions.title: Kubeflow training operator managed by RHOAI through oac-apps
decisions.rejected: The untracked script install made to meet the Sept 1 deadline
decisions.why: Puts the operator under RHOAI and Git on both workload clusters; the custom prod install was removed on 9/24

decisions.title: SRE metrics set for hosted control planes
decisions.why: All measured about 35 times the samples of Telemetry on dev-workload0 (595k against 16k per scrape, 94% of it kube-apiserver); SRE already carries the scheduler metrics that billing needs

discoveries.title: Cross-namespace isolation bypassed using FQDN
discoveries.detail: A tenant could reach another tenant's service by its full DNS name. Short names only appeared to fail because of DNS search paths, not because anything was blocked. Fixed with the three-tier policy design.

discoveries.title: Billing metric absent under Hosted Control Planes
discoveries.detail: kube_pod_resource_request is published only by the kube-scheduler, which under HCP runs on the hub. Since 4.22 the hub scrapes it, but HyperShift's default Telemetry set dropped every scheduler metric. oac-apps e0979f8 (10/2) sets METRICS_SET=SRE on both hubs and the metric now arrives there; forwarding it into the hosted cluster, where the billing code also wants kube_pod_labels, is switched on for dev-workload0 only (3f8532a). Billing generation (#575) has not started, and OAC invoices so far used estimated usage (#462).

discoveries.title: Namespace policy blocked all internet egress
discoveries.detail: The first tenant NetworkPolicy allowed egress only within the namespace, silently breaking pip, git and Go module downloads. Fixed by also allowing egress to 0.0.0.0/0.

discoveries.title: ConnectX-7 NICs are the non-crypto variant
discoveries.detail: No hardware TLS offload, so the CPU pays for all encryption in transit. Matters for NIST, where encryption is mandatory. The crypto-NIC requirement is now in the requirements document for the hardware purchase under negotiation (9/30); who is making the purchase, and whether they have reviewed it, is unanswered.

discoveries.title: Logout does not invalidate the Keycloak session
discoveries.detail: The console session ends but the SSO session persists, so the next login is silent. Needs logoutRedirect pointed at Keycloak's end-session endpoint.

discoveries.title: Object storage proxy deployed on only one cluster
discoveries.detail: Centralised multi-cluster observability needs S3 on the hubs, which needs the proxy there first. Now deployed on both hub clusters and prod-workload0 (9/22); the issue itself is still open.

discoveries.title: NoExecute GPU taints keep OpenShift daemonsets off GPU nodes
discoveries.detail: Many OpenShift components tolerate any NoSchedule taint but not NoExecute, and not all allow custom tolerations. Resolved over several PRs on 9/23; three daemonsets (ingress-canary, insights-runtime-extractor, px-pure-csi-telemetry) still miss a node, judged not operationally significant.

discoveries.title: VM image volumes request Block mode on NFS storage
discoveries.detail: OpenShift Virtualization's OS-image PVCs asked for volumeMode: Block on pure-fb-nfsv4, so they sat Pending, and a Block PVC that does bind cannot be mounted. Setting the storage profile to Filesystem fixed it; oac-apps fa11cb1 puts that in the openshift-virtualization chart, which every virtualization cluster including prod-workload0 receives. Issue closed 9/29; confirmed in config, not on the live cluster.

discoveries.title: Firewall cut idle API and ingress connections after 30 seconds
discoveries.detail: oc logs -f and oc get pods -w on oac-prod-workload0 ended after 30 seconds of silence, because the pfSense HAProxy frontends and backends in front of each hosted cluster kept their 30 s default client and server timeouts. naved001 raised both to one hour on every frontend and backend on 10/5, and schwesig measured all three workload clusters before and after. The setting is now in oac-apps docs/firewall-rules.md with a verify check (e00f769, 9ae79f5); the firewall itself is not in Git, and the issue stays open until the reporter confirms with real workloads.

topology._comment: Every block must be grounded: either "grounding": "repo" (it is visible in oac-apps) or "issue": <n> (it is described in the tracker). build_snapshot.py drops any block that has neither and warns. Blocks whose connections are not described anywhere carry "connections": "unknown" and are drawn unconnected.

datacenter.label: MGHPCC · MOC networks
datacenter.sub: MOC networks in the MGHPCC data centre

hardware_profiles._comment: GPUs per node is a property of the machine and is NOT recorded in oac-apps. Set "gpus": null when the real number is not known - the dashboard will show the pool as 'needs data' and exclude it from GPU totals rather than guess. Fill these in from the inventory in CCI-MOC/open-accelerator-infra.

lenovo-sd650nv2-a100.label: Lenovo SD650 V2 · A100
lenovo-sd650nv2-a100.source: NOT KNOWN - fill in GPUs per node

hub_nodes._comment: Hub clusters are installed with the agent-based installer, so their own node counts are NOT in oac-apps (only hosted clusters declare nodePools there). Fill these in from CCI-MOC/open-accelerator-infra; null renders as 'needs data' rather than 0.

oac-dev-infra.source: NOT KNOWN - compact cluster, control plane and workers colocated

_comment: One-line state-of-the-thread summaries, written by a person after reading the
issue and its comments. Shown in place of the raw last-comment excerpt.
reviewed_at is the date the thread was actually read.

351.summary: Now part of the requirements document for the hardware under negotiation. joachimweyl asks who is doing the purchase and whether they have reviewed it.

470.summary: Fixed on the firewall 10/5: the HAProxy client and server timeouts went from 30 s to one hour on all three workload clusters, measured before and after, and the step is documented in oac-apps. Open only for the reporter to confirm with real workloads.

381.summary: Closed 10/6 with the setup documented in everpure-moc docs/immutable_storage_setup.md. No log bucket exists yet, and naved001 suggests the NIST MVP may use Amazon S3 instead.

520.summary: Deferred: the AWS monitoring investigation and the ColdFront gap analysis take priority.

496.summary: Closed 10/6 after a meeting with the BU storage team; the SOP work that came out of it is tracked in #577.

574.summary: Just opened: whether AWS's Landing Zone Accelerator can cover much of 800-171 instead of implementing controls by hand. bu-renm notes AWS lists compliance mapping for 800-171r2.

569.summary: VMs on oac-dev-workload1 register as agents for oac-dev-infra. After talking with larsks, per-cluster VLAN isolation for virtual clusters is assumed not to be needed for now.

568.summary: Closed 10/6 without a new cluster: tzumainn showed VMs on oac-dev-workload1 can boot the discovery image and register as agents on the hub. Networking is the open part, carried in #569.

555.summary: Closed 10/7: larsks reports every resource on the moc-services cluster is now managed by Argo CD (moc-services-config 80d293c adds the ApplicationSet).

581.summary: tzumainn provisioned MOC-R4PAC08U11-S3 through ESI with RHEL 9.8 on 10/7, with VLAN 439 untagged and 376, 411 and 420 tagged, needed through the end of the year. Open points: one engineer has no SSH key listed, and BMC credentials are not normally given outside the MOC.

18.summary: Closed 9/29: hpdempsey says it was done for the Open Accelerator startups and their projects were created. No requirements list is linked in the thread.

317.summary: The RFC review is done and only sign-off remains; joachimweyl asked msdisme on 9/29 whether it has been signed off, with no answer yet.

536.summary: NIST 800-171 control 3.1.9. Nothing written yet; the next step is to see what BU's existing privacy and security pages can be reused.

499.summary: The checklist is untouched. memalhot has proposed request-form changes: an institutional email, the other users who need access, a project description, and a box for needs beyond the default quota, such as GPUs.

439.summary: The collector is deployed on prod-workload0, but the metrics it needs are not available there. #543 adapts it to the HCP setup, where metrics come from a different endpoint queried per cluster; see #481.

425.summary: Closed. The three H100s have been in prod-workload0 since 9/1, added ahead of requests from two OAC projects that have not firmed up, so there are no expected GPU hours yet.

233.summary: Parked: hpdempsey does not expect to pursue bin-packing for a long time and is leaving it in the backlog, and msdisme was about to move it to the icebox. The July objection stands: no use case is documented, and NIST/HIPAA GPU nodes cannot be shared across organisations.

455.summary: D1 (billing basis), D1b (exceptions) and D2 (idle-reclaim consent) are still with MOC leadership, and the RfD recommends a tier model. New input: vLLM's own request and token counters tell idle from busy without DCGM, per server even on a shared GPU, but only for servers that export them.

540.summary: Closed 9/30 after a redeploy stopped the restarts; no cause was found.

531.summary: Approved 9/30, to be reviewed in November. The A100 for dev-workload0, MOC-R8PAC23U33, is cabled but has no link; a bad cable is suspected with no spares on hand, so the intern project is still blocked.

451.summary: Approved 9/2 by hpdempsey as not billable to Red Hat, capped at 16 A100 GPU hours on the OAC dev cluster; gavin-test is in oac-dev-workload0 user-projects. Closed 9/28 as done.

348.summary: Closed 9/28 by gavinsan33 once the need was met; access came through #451 on the OAC dev cluster.

385.summary: Closed without the upstream change: rather than alter Keycloak's schema to lift the 36-character POLICY_ID limit, computate worked around it in computate-vertx for AI Telemetry.

463.summary: A meeting to review the 800-171 spreadsheet is to be scheduled, and joachimweyl points to a slide deck holding much of the material. The physical-access gaps (separate MGHPCC keyring, access audit, training) are split out to #552.

495.summary: Scope clarified after Heidi questioned static configuration: switches get both a static config (uplinks, VLAN definitions, RoCE) and a dynamic one, with interfaces marked managed left untouched. The driver covers the static half.

310.summary: Closed 9/24 as all set, but not cleanly: the 10.5.1.111 machine then failed to power on (suspected CMOS battery). ajamias is using 10.5.1.15 meanwhile and skanthed is following up with Hakan.

354.summary: Closed 9/17: network testing passed with the new policy. larsks added a chainsaw test suite in oac-apps PR #44, and asanaullah posted the exact allow-intra-namespace NetworkPolicy used.

452.summary: Still waiting on other issues, so msdisme proposes naming the Trustees of Boston University as the Provider for now and rewriting once the entity is settled.

291.summary: Waiting on review and sign-off; msdisme sent a follow-up email on 9/17. No technical dispute recorded.

465.summary: larsks argues LDAP is worth doing regardless of the NIST side. hpdempsey wants it prioritised against the target-cluster work first, and a statement from IS&T on whether they will accept and maintain an LDAP service.

398.summary: Procedural: msdisme has written to BU staff to confirm who can approve and sign off the personas RFC.

501.summary: Opened 9/17. The compliance specifics behind the AWS-versus-on-premises DNS choice are held in the monitoring requirements spreadsheet rather than in the issue.

493.summary: Closed and settled: memalhot ran GPU workloads on the new H100 nodes on 9/22 and they worked, bringing oac-prod-workload0 to five H100 nodes (20 GPUs).

373.summary: Rack R4-PA-C10 was cleared of ESI users on 8/12 and the researchers' remaining hardware left in place. joachimweyl asked on 9/21 whether everyone has what they need so the issue can close; no reply yet.

497.summary: Findings are posted as sub-issues; QuanMPhm will close this once each has consensus on an implementation.

505.summary: Still in progress: the swimlanes were reworked at IS&T's request, and the task is larger than first estimated.

410.summary: knikolla's reading: hosting in AWS us-east-1 is acceptable provided only FedRAMP-authorised services are used — which spawned #508 to enforce that with a service control policy. Not yet confirmed by anyone else, and the second question (can the same IdP serve outside the NIST environment) is left to #413.

413.summary: knikolla's tentative view is that one Keycloak can serve both, isolated by realm (moc and moc-compliance), provided the whole instance is run under the full compliance regime. Explicitly offered as a first reading, not a conclusion.

411.summary: knikolla's tentative answer is yes: CILogon is not FedRAMP, so trusting it pulls it into the boundary and it may not be usable for logging in to CUI clusters. If that holds it cuts against the CILogon federation in the #282 IdP decision; nobody has responded yet.

53.summary: Dormant since July, revived 9/15: the tenant-isolation gap analysis from the ai-ivp review is wanted again, this time to brief the returning Red Hat consultants.

334.summary: On hold until the new firewall appliances are running (10/6 meeting). larsks has widened the issue from LDAP to a general way of exposing moc-services to internal users without a public endpoint.

283.summary: Closed, but joachimweyl is still chasing whether the review and sign-off actually happened — the closure records creation, not approval.

460.summary: Closed. Steps 4-5 are now published at docs.oac.massopen.cloud/model-deployment (content/model-deployment in oac-user-docs).

Still open: who sends outage notices, how to reach customers (joachimweyl counts 3, 4 and 2 contacts for Accelidea, Noah Labs and White Room), actual turnaround times from engineering, and the severity/RCA terms joachimweyl added.

481.summary: METRICS_SET=SRE is merged for both hubs (oac-apps e0979f8) and the scheduler metric now arrives there; forwarding into the hosted cluster is on for dev-workload0 only. The billing code still has to use it (#543, #575).
